keywords.meaning: as expected; impressive; just what I'd expect
keywords.nuance: さすが expresses admiration when someone or something lives up to an existing reputation, expectation, or known ability. It often feels like 'that's exactly what I'd expect from someone like you.'
keywords.exampleTranslation: Just what I'd expect from a teacher.

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Do not confuse さすが with やっぱり. やっぱり means that your expectation was confirmed: 'I knew it.' さすが expresses admiration because someone or something lived up to a reputation or known ability: 'That's exactly what I'd expect.'

questions.hint: The speaker is impressed because Japan lived up to an expectation or reputation.
questions.answer: That's Japan for you. / Just what I'd expect from Japan.

questions.prompt: さすが先生、よく知っていますね。
questions.hint: The teacher knows a lot, as expected.
questions.answer: As expected of a teacher, you really know a lot. / That's a teacher for you.

questions.prompt: 難しい試験だったけど、彼は合格した。さすがだね。
questions.hint: The person succeeded in a way that matches their reputation or ability.
questions.answer: It was a difficult exam, but he passed. That's impressive. / Just what I'd expect from him.

questions.prompt: 彼女は毎日練習している。さすがだ。
questions.hint: The speaker admires her effort or ability.
questions.answer: She practices every day. That's impressive.

productionQuestions.prompt: As expected of a professional, he finished the work quickly.
productionQuestions.hint: Use さすが to praise someone for living up to their professional reputation.

referenceAnswers.answer: さすがプロですね。仕事が早いです。
referenceAnswers.note: Very natural praise. Japanese often splits the idea into two short sentences.

referenceAnswers.answer: さすがプロです。仕事を早く終わらせました。
referenceAnswers.note: More explicit about finishing the work quickly.

productionQuestions.prompt: I knew you could do it. That's impressive.

referenceAnswers.answer: できると思ってたよ。さすが！
referenceAnswers.note: Natural casual Japanese: first the expectation, then the admiration.

referenceAnswers.answer: やっぱりできたね。さすが！
referenceAnswers.note: This naturally contrasts やっぱり ('I knew it') with さすが ('Impressive').

productionQuestions.prompt: That's exactly what I'd expect from you.
productionQuestions.hint: Japanese can often express this with さすが alone.

referenceAnswers.note: Very natural. The person being praised is understood from context.
A casual version used with someone you know well.

productionQuestions.prompt: She's an amazing cook, just as expected.
productionQuestions.hint: Use 料理が上手 or 料理上手.

referenceAnswers.answer: さすがですね。料理が本当に上手です。
料理が本当に上手ですね。さすがです。
referenceAnswers.note: Equally natural with さすが placed after the praise.
